title: LMC region near the Tarantula Nebula
caption: The region around DEM L 299 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: DEM L 299 · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A turbulent region surrounds the ring-shaped nebula DEM L 299 in this view. It lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy that orbits our own, not far from the Tarantula Nebula.

The picture was produced by combining three black-and-white images taken in December 2001 with the Wide Field Imager on the ESO/MPG 2.2-metre telescope at the La Silla Observatory. Each image was taken through a different filter, one in ultraviolet light and two tuned to the glow of oxygen and of hydrogen, and they were then combined into colour.

The coloured rings around some of the brighter stars are not real features in space. They are caused by light reflecting inside the telescope's optics, a common kind of artefact in astronomical images, and they show how the instrument shapes a picture as well as the sky.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.27 x 32.93 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 1,600 × 1,600 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This composite from the Wide Field Imager combines an ultraviolet filter with narrow filters for oxygen and hydrogen light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet part is invisible to the eye, and the coloured rings around bright stars are reflections in the telescope, not something you would see in the sky.
